topics.title: Welcome to kuschonink 98
topics.html:
This is the website of Xiangyin Gu, an artist based in London. It works like a computer from 1998: the work is kept in folders and programs on a desktop. You don’t need to know Windows to use it. Everything opens with the mouse, a finger or the keyboard.

The quickest ways in:

  • Projects: every project, as a folder.
  • The House: the same work, kept in the rooms of a house.
  • About.doc and Contact.

topics.title: The desktop, Start menu and taskbar
topics.html:
The icons on the left of the screen are the desktop. Double-click an icon to open it. On a phone or tablet, tap it once.

The grey bar along the bottom is the taskbar. Click Start for a menu of everything on the site: Programs (each project, the House, About, Contact), recently opened Documents, Settings, Find, Help, Run and Shut Down.

Each open window has a button on the taskbar. Click a button to bring its window to the front; click it again to hide (minimise) the window. Rest the pointer on the clock to see the date. The speaker next to it turns sounds on and off.

topics.title: Using the mouse
topics.html:
• Click an icon to select it. Double-click to open it.
  • Right-click almost anything (the desktop, an icon, a window’s title bar, a photograph, a link) for a menu of what you can do with it. On a touch screen, press and hold instead.
  • Drag a window by its title bar to move it, or drag its edges to resize it. Drag icons to arrange the desktop.
  • Drag across an empty part of the desktop to select several icons at once.

The pointer changes as it did in 1998: an hourglass while something opens, a hand over links. The ghost pointers that follow the mouse are pointer trails; you can switch them off in Control Panel → Mouse.

topics.title: Using the keyboard
topics.html:
Tab, Shift+TabMove between icons, buttons and links
EnterOpen the selected icon or link
Arrow keysMove between desktop icons and menu items; move around the house map
EscClose a menu or a dialog box
Shift+F10 or the Menu keyThe right-click menu for the selected thing
F1This Help (if your browser allows it)
Alt+F4Close the active window (if your browser allows it)

Some shortcuts belong to your own computer or browser (for example Alt+Tab or Ctrl+W); those still do what they normally do.

topics.title: Windows
topics.html:
Every page opens in a window. The three buttons at the top right minimise, maximise (fill the screen) and close it. Double-click the title bar to maximise it or put it back. Windows can overlap: click one to bring it to the front.

Folders and the House have Back, Forward and Up buttons, and an Address bar you can type into, for example C:\kuschonink\image or /house. Your browser’s own Back button works too, and the browser’s address always shows the window in front, so you can share it or bookmark it.

If overlapping windows get in the way, choose Always maximize windows in Control Panel → Display: every window then fills the screen, like an ordinary website.

topics.title: Looking at the work
topics.html:
The Projects folder holds every project. Choose a view: Thumbnails, List or Details. In Details, click a column heading to sort. Select a project to read about it on the left of the window; double-click to open it.

In a project, click a photograph to see it in the Image Viewer, where you can zoom in and step through the photographs. All projects on one page shows everything in one long page.

topics.title: Exploring the House
topics.html:
The site is also a house, drawn from the plans of the 2008 renovation of the family house. Its front, the south façade, has a door and windows you can click.

Inside, the floorplan works like a map: drag to move, scroll (or pinch) to zoom, and change floors with the buttons R, A, 2 and 1 (roof, attic, first floor, ground floor). Type in Search this house to find a room or a project. Tick Blueprint to see the original drawings.

Click a room to open it beside the plan. Every room has a chapter number, an inventory and a table of constraints. Some rooms have furniture with drawers: click a drawer to open it, then an object inside to read it.

One room has no door. It can’t be entered.

topics.title: The rules of the house
topics.html:
The order of the rooms is set by a rule, after Georges Perec’s Life A User’s Manual: a knight moves across the house’s 5 × 5 structural grid, and the rooms are numbered in the order it first lands in them. Lists of sources, times and hidden things are dealt over the grid by Latin squares, and each room shows which of them it fulfils.

Read the Rules of the house, the Index, the Chronology and the Checklist of the chapters.

topics.title: Getting in touch
topics.html: Open Contact to write a message: fill in your name, your email address, a subject and the message, then click Send. You can also write to {email} or follow kuschonink on Instagram.

topics.title: Changing the settings
topics.html:
Open Start → Settings → Control Panel.

  • Display: wallpaper (including some of the artist’s photographs), screen saver, colour scheme (High Contrast is easier to read), and effects such as dragging whole windows.
  • Mouse: pointer trails, double-click speed and larger pointers.
  • Sounds: turn sounds on or off and set the volume.
  • Folder Options: open icons with a single click instead of a double-click.

Settings are kept in this browser only.

topics.title: Starting, logging off and shutting down
topics.html:
The first time you visit in a browser session, kuschonink 98 starts up and asks you to log on. There’s no account: type any name, or none, and press OK (Cancel works too). Click or press any key to skip the start-up screen.

Start → Log Off shows the log-on box again. Start → Shut Down lets you shut the computer down (click to start again), restart it, or put it on stand-by.

topics.title: Troubleshooting
topics.html:
I can’t hear anything.
Click the speaker next to the clock and untick Mute. On an iPhone, also check the silent switch.
I don’t like the pointer trails or the animations.
Control Panel → Mouse → untick Show pointer trails. If your device is set to reduce motion, they’re off already.
The windows are too small, or overlap.
Maximise the window (the middle button at the top right), or choose Always maximize windows in Control Panel → Display.
A page looks wrong.
Click Refresh in the window, or reload the page in your browser.
I’d like the browser’s own right-click menu.
Hold Shift while you right-click.
